elements.element: New York law governs the Agreement.
elements.evidence: Section 11 as rendered: "This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of New York, without regard to the conflict of laws provisions thereof." Only the jurisdiction words were changed from "the Arizona"; the severability sentence and conflict-of-laws tail are retained.

elements.element: State and federal courts in New York County have exclusive jurisdiction over the merits, subject only to temporary injunctive relief elsewhere.
elements.evidence: Section 19 as rendered: Disputes "will be subject to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in New York County, New York." The mandatory USA&M arbitration mechanic and the award-confirmation sentence (which would have permitted enforcement in the federal district of the respondent's residence) are removed, so no competing or foreign forum survives. No alternate-forum carve-out is present at all, which is at least as protective as the permitted temporary-injunctive-relief-only exception; the merits forum is exclusively New York County.

elements.element: The governing law is Delaware, California, or England and Wales.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 11 selects New York law, not Delaware, California, or England and Wales. This is the preferred position, so the fallback level is simply not the level pursued.

elements.element: The dispute forum is the corresponding Delaware or California courts, or the courts of London for England and Wales law.
elements.evidence: Rendered Section 19 designates the state and federal courts in New York County, not Delaware, California, or London courts. Again, the drafter targeted the preferred level.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: New York substantive law plus exclusive New York County state and federal court jurisdiction over all Disputes.

The original clause was a genuine deviation (Arizona law, walk-away-adjacent mandatory USA&M arbitration with confirmation venue keyed to the respondent's residence), so a redline was warranted rather than a rationale-only note.

Minimality holds. In Section 11 only the words "the Arizona" were swapped for "the State of New York"; the severability sentence and the conflict-of-laws tail survive. In Section 19 the deletions (the arbitration submission and the award-confirmation sentence) are the operative arbitration mechanic itself, which had to be converted to reach the courts element, and the heading rename from "Arbitration" to "Dispute Resolution" is required so no dangling arbitration reference remains. No survival tail, fee-shifting, jury waiver, service-of-process, or injunctive-relief boilerplate was added.

Intent preserved: the Dispute definition (common law, statutory and equitable claims, pre- and post-dating the Agreement, limbs (b) and (c)) is retained verbatim, so the breadth of covered disputes is unchanged; only the forum changed. Signature block and Effective Date references are untouched.

Drafting note (not a failure): the retained lead-in "Except as otherwise specified below" now points to whatever carve-outs remain in the un-quoted portion of Section 19; if the deleted award-confirmation sentence was the only "below" exception, delete those four words or confirm a surviving carve-out so the lead-in does not dangle.

No fallback repair is needed, but if Vendor resists New York, the acceptable substitutes are Delaware or California law with the corresponding state and federal courts of that state, or England and Wales law with the courts of London "corresponding" law and forum must move together.
